clue.text: Try, much like it'd come out differently?

definitions.text: Try, much like it'd come out differently?

indicators.note: to come out differently is to turn out in a new arrangement, so these words' letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone urging another attempt, hoping that this time things will turn out otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out differently' shuffles TRY plus MUCH LIKE ITD. The whole clue is also the definition: having another go in the hope that it ends differently is the spirit of the saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying expresses hope that a further attempt succeeds where earlier ones failed, exactly the hopeful retry the clue describes.

clue.text: Vocal way to address Miss Brodie's healthy habits?

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the greeting is heard and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: Miss Jean Brodie, the schoolteacher of Muriel Spark's novel, could be greeted 'Hi, Jean'

explanation.surface: A question about how to greet the famous schoolmistress and her wholesome routines.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Jean Brodie is the teacher in Muriel Spark's novel The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie; 'Hi, Jean' said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits of cleanliness that keep people healthy are what personal care of this kind means.

clue.text: Perhaps Joey Tribbiani's beginning to go off radical

indicators.note: to go off means to leave, so that letter departs from the word for radical

parts.note: a radical in mathematics is a root

indicators.note: beginning picks out only the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Joey Tribbiani, the Friends character, is said to be starting to drop his extreme views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joey' looks like the Friends character but is a baby kangaroo; 'Perhaps' marks a joey as one example of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A joey is a young kangaroo, and the Australian short form names the animal of which it is an instance.

clue.text: Drifter fled to Spain, yes, occupying temporary shelter

indicators.note: occupying means living inside, so the other pieces sit within the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
fled means ran
in Spanish, the word for yes is si

explanation.surface: A wanderer escapes to Spain and moves into a makeshift camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Spain, yes' means 'yes' as said in Spain, SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a person with no fixed home who moves from place to place, a transient person.

clue.text: Painter one attached to steamer held by ship's officer

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the ship's officer wraps round the rest

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

indicators.note: attached to sets the numeral directly before the steamer

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A painter fixes something to a steamer while a ship's officer holds it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' also means a mooring rope, which suits the nautical surface, but here it is the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist, leader of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Vigorous but out of practice, needing a change of hands

indicators.note: hands are right and left, so the right-hand letter is swapped for the left-hand one

parts.note: skills out of practice are rusty

explanation.surface: Someone strong yet rusty, who needs to swap which hand they use.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left): that is the 'change of hands'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty describes someone healthy and strong, full of vigour.

clue.text: Evil lives penned by English poet, mostly it spices things up

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, a pen being an enclosure, so the poet's name surrounds the rest
mostly means not quite all, so the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales
evil can mean ill, as in ill will
lives means is, as in 'he is'

explanation.surface: Wicked lives written up by an English poet, mostly about something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like authorship but means enclosed. 'mostly' cuts CHAUCER to CHAUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot condiment made from fiery peppers adds heat and flavour, literally spicing food up.

clue.text: I want a variable source of income

definitions.note: the clue speaks as the person who wants, so it names that person

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic variable
an earner is something that brings in money

explanation.surface: Someone saying they long for an unpredictable stream of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I want' is spoken by the answer: whoever says it is one who longs for things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who says they long for something is a person with longings, one who pines.

clue.text: Somewhat malign or antagonistic but uninformed

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone a little spiteful or hostile, and also poorly informed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'but uninformed' as the definition; 'but' is only a link word, and the definition is 'uninformed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or information is the plain meaning of both words; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Red extremists literally appear after endless neglect

indicators.note: after puts the extremes behind the shortened word
endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: to shirk a duty is to neglect it
the literal extremes of the alphabet are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Political radicals seem to appear once neglect stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' suggests a communist next to 'extremists', but it is wine; 'literally' means taken as letters, A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiraz is a grape variety making dark red wine, a classic example of a red.

clue.text: Good Detective Inspector abandoning fight over unusual habits

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the remaining letters are read backwards
abandoning means leaving behind, so the inspector is taken out of the fight

parts.note: a dispute is a quarrel or fight
DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A good detective inspector quits a fight about odd behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' looks like behaviour but means clothing. DISPUTE without DI leaves SPUTE; 'over' turns it to ETUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Getups are outfits, especially odd or striking ones; a habit is a costume such as a monk's.

clue.text: Arrests quashing resistance at a higher level, which should cancel an application

indicators.note: quashing means suppressing, so the resistance letter is removed

parts.note: a run-in is slang for an arrest, so arrests are run-ins
R is the physics symbol for resistance
taller means standing at a higher level

explanation.surface: Arrests that suppress resistance from above, which ought to quash a legal application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' looks legal beside 'quashing', but it is a software app. RUN-INS minus R gives UNINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that removes installed programs from a computer cancels them out, undoing their installation.

clue.text: Playpen's devised as means of overhead surveillance

indicators.note: devised means worked out or constructed, so the letters of the word are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A child's playpen has been designed to keep watch from above.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance aircraft fly high to photograph and observe the ground below.

clue.text: Subtlety about match involving Geordies?

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: involving means including within, so the match surrounds the Geordies

parts.note: to fit is to match
Geordies come from Newcastle in the North East of England, so they are NE men

explanation.surface: A careful point about a football match featuring Newcastle fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies are people from Newcastle upon Tyne, in North East England; the question mark flags reading them as NE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement means a fine distinction or nuance, a subtle point.

clue.text: Concerns about interrupting experiment to reveal object in higher space

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the reversed cares split the experiment

parts.note: a test is an experiment

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: concerns are cares or worries

explanation.surface: Worries break into a scientific trial and turn up something in higher dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: CARES read backwards is SERAC, placed in TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tesseract is the four-dimensional analogue of a cube, a hypercube existing in a space beyond three dimensions.

clue.text: European from Bruges after the centre's gone west

indicators.note: west means going right to left, as on a map, so the letters are read backwards
the middle two letters of the Belgian city's name are dropped

explanation.surface: A European from Bruges once the town centre has moved westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUGES without its centre UG leaves BRES, which reads backwards as SERB.
explanation.definitionFit: A Serb is a person from Serbia, a Balkan country in Europe.

clue.text: Permanently writes where Dorothy wasn't any more

definitions.meaning: writing with pen rather than pencil makes the marks indelible
Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz says she is not in Kansas any more; the state's postal code is two letters, K and S, after the word in

explanation.surface: A writer making things permanent, set beside a famous line from The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy tells her dog Toto 'I've a feeling we're not in Kansas any more'; Kansas's US postal code is KS, so the second reading splits as in + Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in ink, rather than pencil, makes the marks permanent, so the verb means writing indelibly.

clue.text: Falls here, enlisted by war against uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards
enlisted by means taken into the ranks of, so the letters lie within these two words

explanation.surface: A soldier falls here, recruited for a war against a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' suggests soldiers dying in war but means waterfalls; the letters run upward through 'war against'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the site of the famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Conversion device managed to get stained in short term

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the shortened word
short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: taken as written before being cut
managed means ran, as in running a business
to smut is to become stained with soot or dirt

explanation.surface: A device that converts things managed to get dirty during a short school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmuter changes one substance into another, a device for conversion.

clue.text: Experiencing enjoyment in a stiff member?

definitions.text: Experiencing enjoyment in a stiff member?

indicators.note: in places the enjoyment inside the stiff piece

parts.note: a rod is a stiff, straight piece
in law, use means the enjoyment of property

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about pleasure and a stiffened body part.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone in this state is stimulated and excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred to excitement, especially sexual excitement, is what the clue's risqué picture describes.

clue.text: Force to work for someone dodgy seen outside facilities

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the toilet
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are arranged unreliably

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for a toilet, or lav

explanation.surface: A shady character seen hanging around outside the public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facilities' is a British euphemism for a toilet. 'dodgy' rearranges the letters of 'seen', which 'outside' wraps round the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone a slave is to compel them to labour in servitude for another.

clue.text: Northern area right in the middle of futile old sea battle

indicators.note: in the middle of puts the right letter inside the word for futile

parts.note: vain means futile

explanation.surface: A sea battle fought pointlessly in the middle of a northern region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Navarino in 1827 was a naval engagement in Greek waters during the Greek War of Independence.

clue.text: Britons wanting borders sabotaged opening

indicators.note: sabotaged means wrecked, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
wanting borders means lacking the outer letters, leaving the inside of the word

explanation.surface: British saboteurs wreck the start of something, lacking borders.
explanation.walkthrough: BRITONS without its outer letters is RITON, which 'sabotaged' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is a brief opening section, as of a song or speech.

clue.text: Jolly Republican wearing First Lady's ring

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so Eve's wraps round the Republican

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible, so the first lady's is Eve's
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A cheerful Republican in the president's wife's ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests the US president's wife, but it is Eve. 'Jolly' is the British intensifier, as in jolly good.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage jolly means very, and the colloquial phrase is a gushing way of saying very.

clue.text: Young bird hunting dog's heading off before end of hunt

indicators.note: before places the shortened dog ahead of that letter
heading off means the first letter goes

parts.note: a beagle is a hound bred for hunting

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter

explanation.surface: A young bird is caught by a hound, which leads before the hunt ends.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAGLE loses its first letter to give EAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a chick of the bird of prey, a young bird.

clue.text: Abduct and execute husband during brief boat trip

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the pieces go inside the short trip
brief means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a sail is a trip in a boat
to hang is to execute

explanation.surface: A villain kidnaps and kills a husband on a short boat outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims the trip's last letter; 'during' puts the execution and the husband inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai someone is to kidnap them, originally forcing men to serve as sailors.

clue.text: Travel over slush

parts.note: to travel is to go
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone sets off across melting snow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is any sticky, sloppy substance, and slush is soft wet mush.

clue.text: Kept cool if stopping broadcast?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the condition fills a gap within the broadcast word

parts.note: something broadcast has been aired
an if is a condition, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Was something kept chilly in case a broadcast stopped?
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms or vehicles cooled by a machine that chills the air are kept cool artificially.
